statement: The CC shall take its boot-loader configuration only from the verified boot-loader image and from signed FIT configurations.
rationale: Defines 'boot configuration' for VE-07. A boot-loader environment read from storage, an interactive console, legacy (unsigned) images or an unsigned FIT configuration would each let storage or console access change what boots without breaking a signature.

statement: The CC shall bind its sealed keys to SHA-256 PCRs 0, 1, 8 and 9 as extended by the boot loader.
rationale: U-Boot v2026.07 extends PCR 0 with its version string, PCR 1 with the devicetree and kernel command line, PCR 8 with the kernel and PCR 9 with the initramfs. Together they identify the boot loader and everything it starts. Later PCRs change at runtime and are left to P4.

statement: The CC shall unseal its keys only under a PCR policy signed with the MSS policy key.
rationale: Keys are sealed once to TPM2_PolicyAuthorize. A legitimate update ships a newly signed policy, so keys are never re-sealed in the clear on a running CC, and nothing on the CC can approve its own boot state.

statement: The CC shall refuse to unseal its keys under a policy whose epoch is below the minimum epoch recorded in its TPM.
rationale: Neither U-Boot v2026.07 nor the Raspberry Pi boot loader enforces anti-rollback. An older, signed but vulnerable chain may still boot; it cannot unseal the WireGuard or signing key, so it cannot join C2.

statement: The CC shall unseal its keys only over a salted TPM session with response encryption.
rationale: A discrete TPM returns unsealed data over its bus in the clear unless the session encrypts it. A captured vehicle (A-08 tier 2) gives an adversary time to attach a bus probe.
